figure: Figure 2.2 (Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge)
issue: Internal numeric inconsistency on the same page: the figure's flat roof is labeled '989 TFLOPS' and the bottom annotation reads 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 -> ridge at 295 FLOP/byte', but the caption's capacity sentence quotes the single-H100 peak as '0.980 PFLOPS'. 989 TFLOPS = 0.989 PFLOPS, not 0.980 PFLOPS (a ~9 TFLOPS / ~0.9% discrepancy, and 980 TFLOPS does not match the house H100 SXM dense spec of 989). The ridge arithmetic confirms 989 is the intended peak: 989e12 / 3.35e12 = 295.2 FLOP/byte, matching the printed '~295'. The conclusion is unaffected (the derived ~1.19 PFLOPS demand exceeds 0.989 just as it exceeds 0.980), but the figure and its caption disagree on the peak value, which violates the book's cross-element consistency standard.
evidence: Figure label (top right): '989 TFLOPS'. Figure bottom annotation: 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 -> ridge at 295 FLOP/byte'. Caption (PDF 43): 'the stated TTFT deadline implies ~1.19 PFLOPS demand, exceeding the compared single-H100 theoretical peak (0.980 PFLOPS)'. Recomputation: 989 TFLOPS = 0.989 PFLOPS; 989/3.35 = 295.2 (ridge consistent with 989, not with 980). 1.19 PFLOPS derives from 2*70e9*9200 / (1.2 s - 0.12 s) = 1.288e15 / 1.08 = 1.193e15, consistent with the TTFT budget on PDF 40 / printed 20.
acceptance_test: Change the caption's '0.980 PFLOPS' to '0.989 PFLOPS' (or '989 TFLOPS') so it matches the figure's own '989 TFLOPS' label and the house H100 SXM dense spec; re-verify the comparison still reads correctly (1.19 PFLOPS > 0.989 PFLOPS, so one H100 is insufficient under the analytical deadline model). Confirm no other caption/figure pair on this page quotes a different H100 dense peak.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — Prefill and decode: two regimes split by the roofline ridge
issue: The roofline is drawn as a single rising line with no horizontal plateau. The compute-bound region (blue, horizontal hatch) is shaded all the way to the top of the plot (1e+15 FLOP/s), but the figure's own annotation states the machine's ceiling is 989 TFLOPS (9.89e14). A reader therefore sees the compute-bound regime as permitting performance up to 1e15 FLOP/s, i.e. above the stated hardware peak. The classic roofline shape (rising ridge + flat ceiling) is missing, and the flat ceiling is the single most important visual fact about the compute-bound regime.
evidence: Rendered page 43: the black ridge line terminates at the top frame near x≈295; to its right the blue 'compute-bound' fill continues to the 1e+15 gridline with no horizontal boundary. The annotation 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte' fixes the ceiling at 9.89e14 FLOP/s, and the floating '989 TFLOPS' text sits at the top of the plot where the plateau should be. The caption's claim that 'prefill sits in the compute-bound regime' is therefore drawn against a region whose upper bound contradicts the stated peak.
acceptance_test: Redraw so that a horizontal ceiling line at 9.89e14 FLOP/s runs from the ridge (AI≈295) to the right edge of the plot, with the compute-bound hatch filling only below that line; attach the '989 TFLOPS peak (BF16 dense)' label to that line. Re-render at 150 dpi and confirm (a) no blue hatch above 9.89e14, (b) the ceiling line is visually continuous with the rising ridge, (c) the prefill marker lies below the ceiling.

issue: The drawn ridge line is geometrically inconsistent with the stated hardware bandwidth. On a log–log roofline the ridge must satisfy y = AI × BW, i.e. slope exactly 1 in log–log, passing through (AI=1, y=3.35e12) and (AI=295, y=9.89e14). As rendered, the line's lower-left endpoint sits at approximately y≈1e12 at AI=1 and reaches 1e15 at AI≈295, which implies BW≈1e12 B/s — a factor of ~3.4 below the annotated 3.35 TB/s. The figure is the book's central quantitative device for the prefill/decode regime split, and a reader who checks the arithmetic against the drawn line will find it does not hold.
evidence: Rendered page 43: black line lower-left endpoint ≈ (x=1 tick, y=1e+12 gridline); upper-right endpoint ≈ (x≈295, y=1e+15). Independently: 989e12 / 3.35e12 = 295.2 FLOP/byte (ridge AI, consistent with the annotation), and the ridge height at AI=1 must be 3.35e12 FLOP/s, i.e. ~0.52 decade above the 1e+12 gridline. The drawn endpoint is ~0.5 decade below that.
acceptance_test: Regenerate the ridge from the annotated constants (y = AI × 3.35e12, capped at 9.89e14) rather than hand-placing endpoints, then verify on the rendered page that the line passes through (1, 3.35e12) and (295, 9.89e14) to within the line width, and that its log–log slope is 1.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — 'prefill' marker (x-position) vs caption and prose
issue: Three different values are in play for the canonical prefill arithmetic intensity, and they do not agree: (a) the caption says the canonical prefill point is '~2K FLOP/byte'; (b) the printed prose on the facing page (printed p.20) repeats 'the canonical prefill point ~2K FLOP/byte'; (c) the figure's 'prefill' triangle is drawn at roughly 4×10^3 FLOP/byte. Worse, ~2K is itself inconsistent with the canonical scenario the book states (70B-class dense model, 1,200 + 8K = 9,200 input tokens): for a dense model, prefill arithmetic intensity ≈ 2·N_params·N_tok / (2·N_params + KV bytes) ≈ N_tok, i.e. ≈9×10^3 FLOP/byte for a 9.2K-token prefill (≈7.8×10^3 if the 24 GB of KV writes are included; ≈9.1×10^3 with attention FLOPs added). A ~2K FLOP/byte prefill corresponds to roughly a 2,000-token prefill, not the canonical 9.2K.
evidence: Rendered page 43: 'prefill' triangle at x ≈ 4×10^3 (between the 1000 and 10000 ticks, ~0.6 decade past 1000). Caption: 'the canonical prefill point ~2K FLOP/byte'. Printed p.20 (PDF p.40): 'the canonical prefill point ~2K FLOP/byte'. Canonical scenario (printed p.20): 70B-class dense, FP16, 1,200 + 8K retrieved context = 9.2K input tokens. Derivation: FLOPs = 2 × 70e9 × 9200 = 1.288e15; bytes ≈ 140 GB weights + 24.1 GB KV write (9200 × 2.62 MB/token) + ~1 GB activations ≈ 165 GB; AI ≈ 7.8e3 FLOP/byte (≈9.2e3 ignoring KV writes).
acceptance_test: Fix one canonical prefill arithmetic-intensity value, state it once in the caption, and place the marker at exactly that x-coordinate (2×10^3 → 0.30 decade past the 1000 tick; 9.2×10^3 → 0.96 decade). Then re-derive it in the text from the canonical scenario (AI ≈ N_prefill_tokens for a dense model) and confirm the prose on printed p.20, the caption, and the marker agree to the stated rounding. If the canonical scenario's prefill length is intended to be ~2K tokens, change the scenario instead and propagate.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — 'roofline ridge ~295' label vs unlabeled black line
issue: The red label 'roofline ridge ~295' sits above the dashed vertical line, but 'roofline ridge' is the natural name for the black diagonal line (the roofline), which is itself unlabeled. A reader can plausibly read the red label as naming the black line, in which case the black line would be claimed to be at AI≈295 — i.e. a vertical line — which is nonsense. The two lines carry two different meanings (a performance ceiling vs. an intensity location) and neither the caption nor the figure disambiguates them.
evidence: Rendered page 43: red text 'roofline ridge ~295' positioned above the plot at the dashed line's x; the black diagonal line has no text label anywhere in the figure or caption. Caption refers to 'the roofline ridge' and 'the ~295 ridge' without saying which drawn element is which.
acceptance_test: Label the black line directly (e.g. 'roofline: y = AI × 3.35 TB/s, capped at 989 TFLOPS') and rename the red annotation to 'ridge AI ≈ 295 FLOP/byte' with a short leader to the dashed line; add one clause to the caption stating that the solid line is the roofline and the dashed line marks the ridge's arithmetic intensity.

issue: The red italic 'decode' annotation is placed immediately adjacent to (and appears to touch or be crossed by) the black roofline line, at the point where the line is steepest. This is the one place in the figure where the reader must distinguish 'the decode operating point' from 'the roofline', and the collision degrades both.
evidence: Rendered page 43: the word 'decode' occupies roughly x∈[178,205] px, y≈315 px; the black ridge line passes through approximately y≈319→310 px over that same x-range, i.e. the glyphs sit on the line's path.
acceptance_test: Move the 'decode' text label to the left of the marker (or below-left, inside the memory-bound region) with clear separation of at least one text-line height from the ridge line, and re-render to confirm no glyph touches the line.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — bottom-left annotation 'H100 SXM, BF16 dense: 989 TFLOPS peak, 3.35 TB/s HBM3 → ridge at 295 FLOP/byte'
issue: This annotation is set in small type directly on top of the diagonally hatched peach memory-bound fill, immediately above the x-axis and beside the '1e+11' tick label. Small dark text over 45° hatching is the lowest-contrast region in the figure, and the annotation is the only place the reader learns the machine constants. It also restates, redundantly and in a second location, the two facts already given by the floating '989 TFLOPS' label and the 'roofline ridge ~295' label.
evidence: Rendered page 43: the annotation runs along the bottom-left inside the plot frame, over the hatch pattern, at a visibly smaller size than the axis labels; the same two numbers (989 TFLOPS, 295 FLOP/byte) appear twice more elsewhere in the figure.
acceptance_test: Move the hardware-constants annotation out of the hatched region — either below the x-axis as a figure note or into the caption — and delete whichever of the two in-figure labels becomes redundant once the ceiling line is drawn (see FIG-2.2-01). Confirm at 150 dpi that the text sits on a plain background with no hatch behind it.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — italic note 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'
issue: This is the figure's most important epistemic caveat — it tells the reader that the two markers are regime indicators, not measurements — yet it is rendered in small, light-gray italic type on the hatched peach fill in the upper-left of the plot. It is the least legible text in the figure and it carries the heaviest interpretive load. The caveat is also not repeated in the caption, where it would be read reliably.
evidence: Rendered page 43: two-line italic gray note at approximately x∈[165,300] px, y≈170–185 px, over the diagonal hatch; visibly lower contrast and smaller than every other annotation. The caption discusses regimes and operating points but does not state that the markers' vertical positions are not measured MFU.
acceptance_test: Set the note in the same size and weight as the other figure annotations, in a dark neutral color, on an unhatched background (e.g. in the white region above the ridge line), and add the equivalent clause to the caption ('the markers indicate regime; their vertical positions are illustrative, not measured MFU').

issue: The '989 TFLOPS' text floats in the upper-right of the plot with no leader line and no boundary to attach to, in the middle of the compute-bound region. issue: The prefill triangle is placed at roughly 5×10^14 FLOP/s, i.e. about half the 989 TFLOPS ceiling. That vertical placement silently encodes a specific assumed MFU (~50%), which the caption does not license and the figure's own note disclaims. evidence: Rendered page 43: triangle at y ≈ 4.9e14 (≈0.31 decade below the 1e+15 gridline), against a stated ceiling of 9.89e14. The caption says only 'prefill lands at high intensity — the compute-bound side'.
acceptance_test: Either place the prefill marker on the ceiling line (making it a pure regime marker) or annotate its vertical coordinate explicitly (e.g. 'illustrative MFU ≈ 50%') and state in the caption that the vertical position is illustrative.

figure: FIGURE 2.2 — color semantics and grayscale behavior
issue: Red carries two unrelated meanings in this figure: the 'decode' marker and the dashed ridge-AI line. In grayscale the decode marker (solid red circle) sits on the peach memory-bound fill and loses contrast against it, and the red dashed line becomes a mid-gray dashed line that could be confused with a gridline. The figure survives grayscale only because shape (circle vs triangle) and dash pattern carry the distinctions; the color assignments themselves do not.
evidence: Rendered page 43: red circle on peach/orange hatched fill; red dashed vertical line; blue triangle on blue hatched fill; blue 'compute-bound' text on blue hatch. Grayscale separation depends entirely on shape and hatch direction (diagonal vs horizontal), which is adequate but not by design.
acceptance_test: Convert the figure to grayscale and confirm that (a) the decode marker is distinguishable from the memory-bound fill, (b) the dashed ridge line is distinguishable from gridlines, (c) the two region labels remain legible on their hatched fills. If any fails, add shape/dash redundancy (e.g. hollow vs filled markers, a distinct dash pattern for the ridge line) rather than relying on hue.

issue: The y-axis is labeled 'attainable performance', which invites the reading that the plotted values are achievable performance figures, while the figure's own note says the markers are not measured MFU and the caption calls the whole thing '[ILLUSTRATIVE]'. The axis is in fact a roofline ceiling, not an attainable-performance measurement.
evidence: Rendered page 43: y-axis label 'attainable performance (FLOP/s)'; figure note 'markers = regime, not measured MFU (real kernels run below the roof)'; caption '[ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual roofline developed in Ch 8'.
acceptance_test: Rename the y-axis to 'roofline ceiling (FLOP/s)' (or 'performance bound (FLOP/s)') and confirm the caption and axis label use the same term for the same quantity.
